story.iWant: logic to select 7-8 relevant narrative questions from the bank based on the user's profiling answers
story.soThat: the main quiz feels highly personalized

subtask.description: In src/lib/profiling/types.ts, define a UserProfile interface that captures the answers from the profiling quiz.
Define the function signature selectNarrativeQuestions(userProfile: UserProfile): NarrativeQuestion[].
Create a mapping between userProfile answers and the demographic tags in the narrative questions.
Implement a scoring or weighting system to prioritize questions with matching tags.
Ensure the function returns a unique set of 7-8 questions.
Handle cases where there are not enough questions with matching tags.
Write tests with mock UserProfile objects to verify that the correct questions are prioritized and selected.
Write a test to ensure the function always returns 7-8 questions, if available.
Write a test to handle edge cases, such as an empty UserProfile.

acceptanceCriteria.ac: The function prioritizes questions tagged with matching demographic indicators.

constraint.description: All logic must be implemented in TypeScript.
The new selection logic should be placed in `src/lib/narrative/selection.ts`.
The function must have the signature `selectNarrativeQuestions(userProfile: UserProfile): NarrativeQuestion[]`.
The function must prioritize questions from the `narrativeQuestions` bank that have demographic tags matching the user's profiling answers.
The function must return a unique set of 7-8 questions.

tests.standards: Unit tests should be written using Vitest. Test files should be co-located with the modules they test, following the pattern `*.test.ts`. Focus on testing the selection logic with various user profiles and asserting that the correct questions are prioritized and returned.

ideas.idea: Write a unit test with a mock `UserProfile` to verify that the `selectNarrativeQuestions` function returns an array of `NarrativeQuestion` objects and that the returned questions have tags that match the user's profile.
Write a unit test to ensure that the function returns a unique set of 7-8 questions, even if there are more than 8 questions with matching tags.
Write a unit test to handle cases where there are fewer than 7-8 questions with matching tags, ensuring that the function still returns a full set of questions by including non-tagged questions.
Write a unit test to handle an empty or incomplete `UserProfile`, ensuring that the function returns a default set of questions.
